items.title: Justice minister says UK must embrace AI now for use in court
items.summary: As reported by the Law Society Gazette, justice minister Sarah Sackman told lawyers at a City of London Law Society conference there was no choice but to embrace AI in the court process, warning the UK risked falling behind other jurisdictions. The Ministry of Justice is developing AI scheduling, transcription and mediation tools. Relevant to housing disrepair firms weighing legal tech.

items.title: Ombudsman finds council left resident in disrepair in temporary accommodation and blocked a suitability review
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman found Birmingham City Council failed to resolve ongoing disrepair for a resident in temporary accommodation and gave conflicting financial information. The resident suffered distress, remained in unsuitable conditions and was denied the chance to ask for a section 202 suitability review.

items.title: Housing Ombudsman annual review shows falling severe maladministration findings as repairs still dominate
items.summary: As reported by the Housing Ombudsman, its Annual Complaints Review for 2025-26 records 8,783 determinations and severe maladministration findings falling to 470, from 714. Repairs featured in 80 per cent of cases, with damp and mould making up 34 per cent of repairs complaints and leaks 23 per cent, and over 75 per cent of both upheld. 4.8 million pounds in compensation was ordered.

items.title: Liberal Democrats push to legislate a 150,000-a-year social homes target
items.summary: As reported by Housing Today, the Liberal Democrats have introduced a private members' bill setting a legal target of 150,000 new social homes a year, described as the missing half of the government's Social Housing Bill. It would give councils control over Right to Buy rules and receipts and create a rent-to-equity route for tenants to build equity from rent payments.

items.title: Updated HHSRS brings fewer hazard categories and a simplified scoring system
items.summary: As reported by the National Residential Landlords Association, the updated Housing Health and Safety Rating System came into force on 23 June 2026 and applies to any inspection started on or after 22 June 2026. Prescribed hazard descriptions fall from 29 to 21, and the former A to J bands are replaced by High, Medium and Low scores, where 1,000 or above counts as High.

items.title: Legal aid firms absorb 10p gap between HMRC and Legal Aid Agency mileage rates
items.summary: As reported by Law Society Gazette, the Legal Aid Practitioners Group says firms are paying the 10p difference between the HM Revenue and Customs mileage rate of 55p and the Legal Aid Agency rate, which remains at 45p. It also says mileage claims must be submitted twice under current guidance, adding unremunerated time for fee earners attending courts and tribunals.

items.title: National Audit Office to investigate resilience of the temporary accommodation system
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the National Audit Office has launched an inquiry into whether the temporary accommodation system delivers value for money, with a report due in Spring 2027. It will examine MHCLG's stewardship and whether the system delivers suitable homes and good outcomes for households. A record 135,600 households were in temporary accommodation in England in March 2026.

items.title: CIH calls on Autumn Budget to fund social homes and tackle temporary accommodation crisis
items.summary: As reported by the Chartered Institute of Housing, its Autumn Budget submission urges government to build and retain more social housing, free councils from historic Housing Revenue Account debt, and tackle the temporary accommodation crisis. It cites 134,210 households in temporary accommodation and seeks Local Housing Allowance rates matching true rental costs.

items.title: Social Housing Bill receives Second Reading in the House of Commons
items.summary: As reported by the Chartered Institute of Housing, the Social Housing Bill receives its Second Reading in the House of Commons on 10 September 2026, having completed its Lords stages. The bill would reform the Right to Buy, require four weeks notice before a private registered provider sells a social home, and strengthen protections for tenants who are victims of domestic abuse.

items.title: PRS database opens for landlord registration from 15 December at 65 pounds per property
items.summary: As reported by the National Residential Landlords Association, registration on the new private rented sector database opens from 15 December 2026 in a 12-month rollout starting in the West Midlands. Landlords in England pay 65 pounds per property per year and must register all homes by 14 November 2027. Penalties run to 7,000 pounds, or 40,000 pounds for repeat breaches.

items.title: Scottish Government publishes Awaab's Law guidance for tenants in Scotland
items.summary: As reported by Scottish Government, Awaab's Law comes into force in Scotland on 6 October 2026, with earlier cases outside its timeframes. Landlords must investigate damp or mould reports within 10 working days, give written findings within 3, and begin repairs within 5. It applies to Scottish Secure, Short Scottish Secure and most private tenancies.

items.title: Foreign lawyer struck off after submitting AI-generated false case citations at the SDT
items.summary: As reported by Law Society Gazette, a foreign lawyer who used AI-generated false case citations in a written defence before the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal was struck off. The tribunal, considering such citations for the first time, warned it would take a hard line on lawyers misleading proceedings through AI. A reminder to housing disrepair specialists to verify case law sourced from AI.
